source-text.rule: A code fact is READ FROM SOURCE TEXT, so it must name at least one anchor: the span it was read from. An unanchored code fact names no file that could have been read and is refused (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`). This was previously enforced only inside the syntax-universe capability guard, so the same unanchored `declares` or `references` fact closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe; the law is one law and now binds in every universe.
source-text.noIdentityEqualityPromise: There is deliberately NO ADDITIONAL relation-specific maximum and no canonical extent BEYOND THE COMMON SCHEMA BOUNDS - foundation fact.anchors already carries maxItems 100000 and uniqueItems, and those continue to apply to every relation. An earlier revision said there is no upper bound at all, which contradicted that global bound; what this class declines to impose is a per-relation ceiling or a canonical span set, not the shared one. Which spans a producer cites for a multi-span claim is a genuine semantic choice about what was read, so two conformant producers that cite different spans have produced DIFFERENT semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different fact2 identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts, and asserting one would be a false equality between two different pieces of evidence.

body-identity.rule: Unchanged from the existing `bodyIdentityJoin.anchorCardinality`: exactly the body span the identity is over. Zero would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice.

inventory.rule: An inventory fact is NOT read from a source span. Its whole semantic input is its payload, and that payload is already bound to the snapshot by this relation's own `snapshotJoins`: the path must be in the snapshot inventory, and for `file` the content digest, the byte length and CUSTODY of the exact retained bytes are joined as well. An anchor could only restate a subset of a claim that is already joined, and because nothing derives it, it is a free axis that gives one semantic input several spellings and several identities. It is therefore closed at zero (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
inventory.whatThisMakesRepresentable: Exactly zero is the only cardinality every inventoried path can satisfy, which is what makes the unconditional inventory promise honest: a path no bundled grammar reads (`tool/main.py`), an extensionless path (`LICENSE`), a data-document path, and - decisively - a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is by construction NOT in the analysed snapshot and can therefore carry no anchor at all. A cardinality of one would make that last case unrepresentable and would newly require the manifest bytes of every `package` fact to be retained, neither of which any contract asks for.
inventory.whatItAlsoCloses: The `file` row's `anchorPathField` was the only defence against an arbitrary anchor borrowed to satisfy an inventory claim, and it covered `file` alone: on frozen v13 a `package@manifest-declared` fact claiming `package.json` closed a Run while anchored into an unrelated `a.ts`. Closing the class at zero refuses that for all three inventory relations with one reason. `anchorPathField` is retained as the narrower per-row statement it always was; under this cardinality it can no longer be reached for `file`, and that is the point - the broader law subsumes it rather than leaving a predicate whose only remaining reading is the vacuous one.
inventory.rawByteBoundary: An inventory claim retains path, content digest and byte length WITHOUT anyone decoding the bytes. At zero anchors the ANCHOR_SOURCE/ANCHOR_RANGE/ANCHOR_UTF8 checks never run for such a fact - they iterate the anchors - while the inventoried-file join still does, and it only hashes and measures. An EMPTY file and a NON-UTF8 BINARY file are therefore ordinary inventory, at an extensionless path as readily as any other; requiring bytes to parse as code or as UTF8 merely to record their path and hash would narrow the promise. The source-text and body-identity classes keep exactly the scope they had: the SAME non-UTF8 bytes still refuse as a code-span anchor (ANCHOR_UTF8), and the digest, length and path joins still refuse a wrong claim about those bytes.
inventory.locationRouteAfterRemovingAnchors: Removing inventory anchors removes NO location route, and none is invented to replace them. Nothing reads fact.anchors as a finding location: a finding locates through finding-fingerprint.subjectKey.logicalPath, an inventory claim's own location is its payload path joined to the snapshot inventory by this relation's snapshotJoins, and finding, finding-fingerprint, proof-bundle and predicate-witness carry no anchor field at all. A finding over a zero-anchor inventory fact closes a Run and is located by exactly those existing records.

membershipRule: A resolution is admissible for a relation only if it is a member of THAT relation's `ladder`. A rung that is a member of another relation's ladder is refused, not accepted as a live vocabulary token; the flat rung vocabulary published elsewhere is necessary but never sufficient. Order comparison is the index within one relation's ladder; nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another, and there is no global rank.
rungsAreFieldRulesNotTheLadder: `rungs` is a different table: the per-rung required/forbidden PAYLOAD FIELD rules. It is legitimately the empty object for a relation with no per-rung field variance, which is every single-rung relation. Reading `rungs` as the ladder is the defect this key exists to prevent: an empty field-rule table must never be read as an absent ladder, and never as a licence to skip ladder membership. Membership is checked against `ladder`, always, with no fallback.
subjectKindLaw: What a subject-scope's `subjects` entries IDENTIFY, per relation. `source-path`: each subject is a path in the snapshot this scope names, so the scope's own extent is exactly those paths - `file` and `vcs-change` bind it through their registry snapshotJoins pathField, and `clones` binds it through bodyIdentityJoin, whose single anchor IS the body span the identity is over. `package-name`: a package identifier, not a path. `symbol`: an opaque SubjectIdV1 that the record associates with no path; the enumerator's attribution of symbols to files is trusted and is NOT re-derivable from the retained Run, so no per-subject path law is possible for these relations and any capability question about them can only be answered at the coarser retained extent. That limit is stated rather than worked around: inventing symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence.
